newsitem.title: USA: U.S. March T-bond futures finish sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. March T-bond futures finish sharply lower.

text.p: U.S. March Treasury bond futures finished sharply lower in a session of heavy trade before the November jobs report Friday morning.
A Reuters survey of Wall Street economists forecast November jobs up 179,000, compared with 210,000 in October. The unemployment rate is seen unchanged at 5.2 percent.
As talk spread that the risk for November was stronger jobs growth than forecast, bond futures broke down through several key support levels.
Some traders pointed to the Liscio Report, which foreacst a November jobs gain of 215,000.

March collapsed from a session high of 115-12/32 to a more than two-week low of 113-29/32. Traders said March easily peeled away support at the earlier session low of 114-26/32, at 114-20/32 and at old hourly lows of 114-2/32 to 114-4/32.
Support held at 113-24/32, approximately the 6-1/2-percent cash yield equivalent.

"It actually started a couple of days ago," said Don Pullen, trading floor bond manager for E.D. and F. Man. "I think traders this week were looking for reasons to take profits before the number on Friday," he said. "It's the big number between now and the end of the year."
He said selling was persistent all day, and said the losses set the stage for more of a correction in bond futures.
If traders believe this is the correction from 9-1/2-month highs that many have been looking for, he said losses could continue into next week, with support at 112-00.
"We could see more losses as the market continues to correct overbought conditions," Pullen said.
Traders cited talk of cash Treasury selling by foreign entities and said the lack of a Fed coupon pass and a weaker U.S. dollar also weighed on the market.
But many said the bulk of the losses were technical, with panic-type selling exacerbating the dim tone.
"When we took out 114-22/32, we turned the trend down for the first time since October," said Jim Hyerczyk, technical analyst with JAH Research and Trading.

March T-bonds closed down 1-08/32 to 114-3/32, 10-year notes fell 21/32 to 110-14/32, five-year notes were down 25/64 at 107-35/64, March T-bills fell three basis points to 95.01 and March Eurodollars were down four at 94.48.
